headline: ag-grid-a11y-test helps developers find accessibility issues in data grids
summary: A new helper tool, ag-grid-a11y-test, integrates with Jest and Playwright to identify accessibility problems in complex data grids.
details: Dense data grids, common in applications, often hide accessibility issues that can make them difficult for users with disabilities to navigate. Standard accessibility tools may not catch grid-specific problems, such as correct row count exposure or keyboard navigation.

To address this, a new helper tool called ag-grid-a11y-test has been developed. It builds upon existing tools like axe-core, adding grid-aware checks tailored for AG Grid's structure and common markup patterns.

Currently in an early alpha preview and available on GitHub, ag-grid-a11y-test allows developers to integrate grid-specific accessibility testing into their workflows. The findings are categorized by severity: error, warning, and info, prompting developers to investigate potential issues.

The tool can be installed locally by cloning the GitHub repository and building a package. Examples demonstrate how to use it within Angular projects, merging findings from axe-core and the grid-specific rules into a single report.

While jsdom can be used for testing, a real browser environment is recommended for the most reliable results, especially for testing keyboard interactions. Future planned work includes integration tests for various AG Grid versions and expanded keyboard flow testing.
The developer encourages feedback and contributions, inviting users to report issues or submit pull requests on GitHub. The tool is not officially affiliated with AG Grid.

headline_marked: Sonos [[voice assistant]] Sonos 27voice launches in early access Nov. 6
headline: Sonos voice assistant Sonos 27voice launches in early access Nov. 6
summary: The new assistant understands natural language and answers general knowledge questions, aiming to avoid the backlash of the company's previous app redesign.
details: Sonos has announced that its new voice assistant, Sonos 27voice, will be available to test in early access starting November 6. This update is rolling out this week as part of a larger software update, Sonos 27.

Unlike previous voice control features, Sonos 27voice is designed to understand natural language requests and answer general knowledge questions, similar to modern AI assistants. It can control playback, set timers, interact with smart home devices, and provide current weather information.

Users can ask the assistant to play music based on mood or genre, or even identify specific albums like "that Bowie album about an adventure in space." It aims to offer a more intuitive and comprehensive experience than older voice control systems.

To gain early access, users must request it within the Sonos app and be approved. Sonos is testing the feature with a limited group before a full 2027 release, likely to gather feedback and prevent issues similar to its problematic 2024 app redesign.
The early access for Sonos 27voice is currently limited to the US and only supports English. The Sonos 27 software itself is compatible with hardware running on the company's S2 platform.

Alongside the voice assistant, Sonos 27 also introduces 'Presets,' allowing users to save and instantly recall specific music and playback settings. Additionally, 'System Health' for iOS users provides an overview of system status, flagging potential issues with speaker connections or Wi-Fi.
